utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: While the witness is being brought into court, let me deal with the Prosecution's motion to amend the date for the testimony that was projected by videolink conference later this week. It's proposed now that that should be the week of the 27th of November. I take it there's no Defence objection to that. Therefore, we will authorise the change, and in doing so, we will include in the order authority to the parties to reach agreement on varying the date for any videolink testimony in future so that it doesn't need to come back to the Chamber unless there is controversy between the parties. And each time we do grant an order for videolink testimony, that provision will be included in the order to avoid this situation being repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zyrapi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your evidence will now continue. Please remember that the solemn declaration you made at the beginning of your evidence to tell the truth continues to apply to your evidence today. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, good afternoon. Mr. Zyrapi, yesterday we finished off discussing uniforms used by the KLA, and I'd like to move on to some related topics about the equipment used by the KLA. First, if we could go through the kind of weapons that the KLA used. Could you describe the weapons that the KLA had, maybe starting with personal weapons of individual soldiers and then move up to heavier weapons.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The KLA used these kinds of weapons, starting from personal weapons, such as pistols, AK-47s or Kalashnikovs, which were of different makes, Chinese, Albanian, former Yugoslav. Then they used semi-automatic rifles, which made up 70 to 80 per cent of the weaponry used. Then there were light machine-guns of the calibre 7.9 and 7.62. I can't remember. I don't know the exact number of these weapons. Then 20 -- correction, 12.7-millimetre heavy machine-guns. I do not know the exact number of these guns. Anti-tank weapons, RPGs, with a range of 150 to 500 metres. There were also Zoljas. There were only a few of them because it was difficult to find them. Some of them used mortars, 82-millimetre mortars. I don't know the approximate number of these mortars, but I know that there were just a few of them and only a few shells, maybe only five to 10 shells per mortar. There were only two 120-millimetre mortars. One was used in the Llap zone and the other in the Berisha mountains. In addition, there were other weapons of various calibres. I don't know the exact number. There were a few recoilless guns, cannons, but just a few of them. As I said, I don't know the exact number. But as far as I know, these were generally the weapons that were used by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did individual soldiers also have, for example, grenades, hand-grenades they could use?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did, hand-grenades. An average number of grenades would be two or three grenades per soldier. That would be the average number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did the KLA also possess mines; in that case, if that is the case, what kind of mines?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult to transport mines. There were only very few anti-tank mines. As I said, it was very difficult to transport them. It was either the choice of carrying them on one's shoulder or using horses, so it was difficult. They were very heavy. I don't know how many there were, but very few I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What was the -- sorry, maybe we should just clarify. What is a Zolja?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Zolja is a hand-held mortar. It's a kind of RPG, 64-millimetres. It's a single-use weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did the KLA obtain its weapons from, if you can describe that.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons, and especially ammunition, was obtained from Albania mostly, so the majority came from Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was it imported into Albania by the KLA, or had you -- or was it just purchased in Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was imported from other countries as well, but the majority of them were purchased in Albania because there were factories there such as weapons of 7.62-millimetre calibre. Those were obtained from Albania itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move on to communications equipment. Generally, what kind of communication did you use during your time as Chief of Staff of the KLA to communicate with units on the ground in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, our communications within the KLA were done through radio, Motorolas, or satellite telephones, but we also used couriers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then transport, you talked about carrying mines on horses or on individuals' backs. But apart from your feet, did you possess other means of transport?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, it was very difficult to transport things, and the soldiers used to either carry the weapons on their backs or use horses, while, within the territory of Kosova, we used private vehicles, trucks, buses. These vehicles were mostly used in the areas that were not under Serb control until March. After March, it was difficult to use them, so most of the transportation was done on foot or using horses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, in relation to communications, when you talk about Motorolas, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I speak of Motorolas, these are hand-held radios that we called Motorola, but those were mainly of Motorola make. But there were also other makes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And satellite telephone, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I speak of satellite telephones, this means telephones that use satellite for communication, satellite waves, not the normal mobile phones. That was a very secure way of communicating between the staff and the various zones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe I should have completed the picture a little bit more on the Motorola radios. What is the range of a Motorola radio, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the radios were mainly in the possession of the commanders of the zones or brigade commanders, but their range was not very large one; it was only a few kilometres. So sometimes we could not communicate with those radios, if people were very far. Sometimes their range reached up to 50 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did the KLA possess any relay stations which would enable you to increase the range of these kinds of radios?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't. There was only one in Pastrik area. There was a repeater in the Pastrik area which increased the range of communication, but that was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, we earlier touched upon training activity, and at one point you were responsible for that part of the training. I'd like to show you some material in that regard, but before I do that, could you just repeat for the court, please, what were the main kinds of training that were given to KLA forces during your time as Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From January to March, the staff was conducting training, and this training was focused on use of weapons, training commanders and officers from the lowest level to the battalion level, and also preparation for operations and combat actions at these levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like if we could see Prosecution Exhibit P2459, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And as the case was with some of the documents yesterday, is it correct that this is also a document that you provided to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, generally, this bundle of material, what is that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a document that was used as an example in the training of the commanders - company commanders, battalion commanders - and we used these examples to train them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the first -- the sheet we see now on the screen, what is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I should indicate to the Court that we do have a translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, this is a document that was used in the training of officers. "Combat Activities" is the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Looking at the English translation, I can see that it has a number of blanks. Is it essentially a template that could be used subsequently by officers? The sheet we see now, what's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a kind of template, a form that was used by the officers of various ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zyrapi, this particular document that you just described briefly - I think we can zoom out again; I'm not going to show any of the specific text - but what is this document, and how did this fit into the training? What kind of training?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: We don't have the translation into English of these documents.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is also a form that was used in the training of battalion commanders. It's a document. It's a plan for the commander observation on this date. The date is blank. And it describes the way -- how to observe the terrain before carrying out operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, when a document comes up on the e-court, do the interpreters not have access to it on e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think the problem for the Albanian translators is that they do not have access to it, but maybe they can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ah, so it's one booth that doesn't have access, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: No booth has access to e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's contrary to the information we were given earlier in the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Anyway, we have to proceed, obviously, on the basis that they don't for the moment, in which case you really should give a hard copy to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We will make an effort to do that. And with the remainder of this document, we're not going to go into --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- much of the text, so I think we can get by. If we can go two pages further on in this document, please. Sorry, only one page on. So go to the next page. My apologies. We need to go one page back now. We need to go to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I think it reads someplace on the heading here, it reads, "To the Commander." Could I get you to just read out that part of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. "To the Commander." Under that is: "Order to Attack," then number, operative number, and there is a blank. Then "Section." It's the scale of the map that it refers to, 1:200.000 and 1:50.000. Then it describes the territory in the municipality of Malisevo, the road Malisevo to Orllat. "The enemy is positioned in this order," and it goes on to describe where the enemy forces are. Number 2 relates to the units, our units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And this format, would that also be the standard format of a combat order then used by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was used in the training as well, but it was issued also later on, while carrying out actions. They were used as forms that would be filled with regard to operations. This is an example of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The bit that's missing from this appears to be the map references.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, you gave the different -- the scales of the maps, and then it says "Buqimit [phoen] ..." Why is that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand the question. There was an interruption in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry. It seems as if there is no indication of what map is being used in connection with this particular document. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map reference is not here because this is just an example, and the part that is a blank, the "...", that would be filled later on. In case of military operations, that would be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, again, this is because this is a template that could be used in the future. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to move to page 5 of this same exhibit, please. My apologies, my notes are wrong. We'll need to go to page 6. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, what is this document? If you could just very briefly describe that.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was also used as a sample during the training of the officers. It's a plan of engagement of the zone -- operative zone commands, and this particularly deals with Pastrik on the D day. It's just a sample, as I said. And this describes the duties of each sector in this operative zone, when they had to be engaged and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then if we can just go to the last page of this exhibit. This time I got it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zyrapi, this last page of the bundle, what is this, and what does that -- what is this?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a sample document that was used during the training. It's a document that speaks about the engagement of units in various territories. In this concrete example, it speaks about the municipality of Prizren, and then it says who gives the order. Then it says, "Order." Then number 1 speaks about the unit that receives their order, deployment of troops, the aim of the deployment, and further explanation about this order to deploy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. I will move now back to the situation in Kosovo or the situation on the ground. Could you describe the military situation in Kosovo in the winter 1998/1999?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in 1998/1999, during the winter period, the military situation as far as KLA forces are concerned in Kosovo were in development. The training and their preparation was going on from lowest levels to the highest level. For example, the KLA followed this example and that's how it prepared for further action, for the further -- in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How about fighting? Was there any fighting during this period?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember there were combat operations in the Nerodimlje operative zone in January. There were no major-scale combat activities in other areas at that time. And after March, when the NATO air-strikes begin, the combat activities began to increase.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Before getting to the situation after the NATO bombing, you said there were no, I think you said, major-scale combat activity. Were there more localised combat activities up until the NATO bombing started?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very small ones, I would say. I mentioned some in January, even in Pastrik area, the activities in Recak village. There was also smaller activities in Prizren area, in Drini valley, but no, as I said, major-scale combat activities during this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was there any offensive -- offensive -- sorry, offensive combat activity on the part of the KLA among these smaller incidents you've referred to?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no big offensive on the part of the KLA at that time. They were actually defending themselves in those territories where smaller-scale combat activities were going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: During this period, were there attacks on roadblocks or ambushes or that kind of smaller operations, or not during this time period?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such operations, attacks on check-points, that constituted a kind of obstacle for our forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This seems there was -- it seems you gave quite a long answer. It was translated as, "there were such operations, attacks on check-points, that constituted obstacles to our forces." I don't know. Did you give more explanation than that? Otherwise, I'll just follow up with some questions, but I just wanted to be clear on that.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was there were attacks on check-points, check-points that constituted an obstacle for our forces during the movement, and that's why they were attacked. But these attacks were not of a great intensity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when you say they constituted obstacles, in what sense did they constitute obstacles? Obstacles to what?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a sense that they constituted an obstacle when the brigades were moving from one zone, let's say, to another. That's why the check-points in relevant areas were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You also described smaller-scale operations of a more defensive nature. How did they come about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The smaller-scale operations, for example, in Nerodimlje operations zone, the attack of the Serb forces on Recak village, our forces were used -- were engaged in defensive action. In addition, in Prizren area, in Drini valley, the KLA forces were also attacked. And this is when the KLA forces were engaged again in defensive action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like now to move on to the period after the beginning of the NATO bombing. Maybe we can start with the days just before the NATO bombing started. Could you describe the military situation as you saw it at the time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, and pursuant to the reports from the terrain, at that time there was a lot of movement by the Serb forces. They moved in different directions and took positions in different areas in the territory of Kosova. They were deployed even before the NATO attacks, but now I'm speaking about the time around the time when the NATO air-strikes began. The KLA forces did not move a lot. They were in a state of readiness and followed the movement of the Serb forces and their positioning. So they followed their movements, they were in state of readiness, and they took up defensive positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then once the NATO bombing started, what happened?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once the NATO bombing started on the 24th of March, at around 9.00 p.m., that's when the NATO air-strikes began, and immediately -- an hour or an hour and a half after the NATO bombing, the Serb forces launched an artillery attack on KLA positions. In the early morning hours on the 25th, the Serb forces also launched other attacks on territories controlled by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like us now, if we could -- call it up so we can see it, Exhibit P2447, and then I think we'll need the usher to assist in distributing something from that document. What we have done is, this is a map that has been marked by the witness. As it doesn't come up so clearly in the e-court, we have printed out a part of that exhibit and blown it up, and then we have marked some letters that were indicated by the witness on the map in a clearer form. Yes. We have for the usher another copy we can put on the ELMO. Maybe the witness could be given a pen in case he would like to point to the map. Well, maybe what we should do -- we cannot zoom just a little bit more out. We might have made the copy a little bit too big for the equipment. Okay. I think that will do for our purposes. I think that is fine, as everybody also has copies. It should be working fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, on this map there are two areas -- well, we have two areas indicated. One is an area on the upper part of the map indicated by E, F, G, and on the lower part, we have A, B, C, and then we have an area marked with a D. Those areas, what are they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Though this scale is very small for me to be precise in defining the line, these areas designate the territories that were under the control of the KLA up to the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, before the NATO bombing started on the 24th of March, the KLA held -- well, approximately, but held the areas you have indicated on the map. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, did the KLA also hold areas in other parts of Kosovo but which you have not marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like, first, if you could explain the chronology from the 24th, from when the NATO bombing started and the following days, and if we could concentrate first on the area marked with A, B, and C. So before the NATO bombing started, in this area, A, B, and C, were you present in that area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I visited earlier, before the NATO bombing started. These were the positions and zones controlled by the KLA up to the 24th of March. As I said earlier, once the bombing started, an hour or two later, the Serb forces launched an artillery attack on positions in a territory marked with A, "KLA positions." Subsequently, in early morning hours on the 25th of March they launched other attacks. They launched their attacks from the direction of Rahovec on the villages of Nagavc and Hoce, and Nishor. Considering the concentration of Serb forces in this territory from earlier, in the area starting from Pirane and up to the Gjakova junction and Bellacerkva, the attacks that were launched early in the morning of 25th of March, there was combat activity. I want to mention this: Before the artillery attack started -- correction. After the artillery attacks started, we wanted the population in this area to move out for security reasons. The KLA forces, together with the population, began to withdraw. The population in Randubrava was withdrawn and sheltered in Mamusa village. There was no KLA presence in this village before, not even KLA positions. It is inhabited by Turks, people of Turkish ethnic group. The village of Reti Ulat also was moved out and withdrawn in the direction of Mamusa. I'm still speaking about the 25th of March. The KLA also withdrew sometime in the afternoon on the 25th, in Kolobar, and left in the direction of Neprebishte village, Samadraxhe village, and moved to the territory of Doberdolan village. Why our forces withdrew in this direction, it was because the attacks were launched in the direction of Rahovec, Suhareke. That's why the KLA withdrew to the mountainous area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you. So the area indicated by a B, when were the KLA forces established there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Starting from the 25th and the 26th. So all forces that were in the territory marked with A, when this attack was launched, there were two brigades here engaged in defensive actions, 124th and 125th Brigade. As I said earlier, these forces withdrew in the afternoon hours, together with the population to Doberdolan village. However, the combat was still going on from the direction of Rahovec and Suhareke, towards Samadraxhe village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so the front line towards Orahovac and the front line towards Suva Reka -- my colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting, but, with your leave, I have one thing to say. We followed the testimony closely, but we cannot clearly see the directions he was showing. Perhaps we have the technical means for showing that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You mean we could turn the map the right way up?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A technological innovation into practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure that would solve the problem because I don't think the areas that are being mentioned are on the map. But we can try this, for starts. We then need to move the map up. Upwards, please. There we are. I think Mr. Fila is waving to you. Would you like to move in further? I think we're fine here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, what KLA units were on the front towards Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Rahovec you can see the village of Opterush here, and here, in this area, this is where the 124th Brigade of the Pastrik Operational Zone was. From this part here and up to here was the 125th Brigade of the Pastrik Operational Zone. Here, in Neprebishte, there was some units of the 123rd Brigade. So these were the units that were in this area. The units of the 123rd Brigade then continued along this front line here, which goes through Studencan, Pecan, Sllapuzhan, and you can see where the line ends between Blace and Temeqin. And here begins the area of 121 Brigade, which was deployed in the defensive positions here in this area above Blace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You said that the civilians and the two brigades were withdrawing together. Could you explain how this removal of the civilians worked in practice? Did they move all together in one group, or how did it work?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in practice this was the case. First, from Randubrava, they withdrew in the direction of Reti or Kolobar village and went to Mamusa village. The units were waiting for the population to withdraw first, and afterwards, once the population was withdrawn, they went to Reti. The population that that withdrew from Reti, Opterush, Neprebishte, Samadraxhe, Studencan, went in the direction of Doberdolan. Some from Neprebishte and Studencan village went in the direction of Mamusa, but the majority went towards Pagarusa where they withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And there's a line between the area A and B. What does that line indicate?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The line between A and B denotes where the forces were withdrawn, 125th, 124th and 123rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when were they -- when were they at that line?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it is shown on the map, this line goes above the village of Doberdolan, includes the hills and Sematishte villages, and the hill above Pecan village. This is the situation at that time, on the 25th and 26th of March. The attacks were continuous at that time, the attacks that I mentioned earlier, one from the direction of Suhareke and the other from the direction of Rahovec on Opterusa, Samadraxhe, Studencan and Doberdolan villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm struggling to see Doberdolan. Can you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We have one of these problems of multi-lingual maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're on what I assumed it was. It's written Doberdol.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Doberdol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, there's also a line between the areas B and C. Just so we get the overview, what is that line, if we first could set that out.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the line through which the Brigade 125, 24 and 23 withdrew. So the population that withdrew from the villages in the A area moved to the area marked with B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are markings of two colours on the map. Now, it's not clear to me exactly what we're referring to. Are the orange markings simply showing boundaries of areas, or do they signify something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, it might be more simple: First, the red markings, what are they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orange markings show the front line, the line where the KLA forces were positioned, while the red lines represent the Serb forces and the direction of their attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The line that you have made between the areas B and C, when did the KLA forces arrive at that line?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between zone B and C you can see here the front line. All these units that I mentioned earlier, the three brigades, and part of the 122nd Brigade were withdrawn here around the 31st of March, because the front line here was penetrated on that date in Gajrak. That's why they started withdrawing on that day, because this point fell and this endangered both the military people, our forces, and the population. So the population and the forces from the B area went towards the Berisha mountains, here in C. This happened in the early hours in the morning, on the 1st of April. The forces and population were positioned in this area here that I marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like, if we can see now in -- we'll swap the screen over so we can see an exhibit for a moment, Exhibit P2457, please. We do have an English translation of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, do you now have a document in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We have an English and an Albanian version, I think, up now, at least on my screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, can you see the document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is that a document, again I'll have to ask you, that you provided to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where did you get that document from?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the archives of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order for combat operations. It is addressed to the commander of the Pastrik Operational Zone. It speaks about the withdrawing of the KLA forces. It says where these forces should withdraw to, which front line, in order to organise their defence. Number 2, form a group, and who would be the commander of the group, because there would be three brigades in this area, so who would be the leader of the whole number of forces. Then number 3 says that the population should withdraw from Bellanice to Ngucat. And then also the deployment of the military hospital. It was in the B area we saw in the map, in Pagarusa, and it says which direction should the military hospital go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if we can just scroll down a little bit so we can see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This is an order issued by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order issued by me. It's signed and stamped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, if we go back to the map again which is on the ELMO. The line described in this order, does that correspond to the line between B and C, or is that a different line that you ordered to be established?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This order refers to this line here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: To the orange line between B and C, approximately; is that correct? Or part of that.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So when that line was established, if I can see the map correctly, was the line running through the village of Bellanice or outside the village?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was above the Bellanice village. You can see from the map here. It doesn't run through Bellanice. It's above. You can see the village Ngucat here, and then towards Temeqin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And in your order [Realtime transcript read in error "around"], you say that the civilian population should move. Did the civilian population actually move?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, the population in Bellanice did not obey the order and they remained in that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, why did you order the population in Bellanice to move?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order for the withdrawal of the population from Bellanice, but also other villages, was given for security reasons, for the security of the population, so that they wouldn't have any problems in case of fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I need the assistance of the usher now. Well, let's see if we can cover --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Fighting about what? What were you hoping to gain here by fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we were hoping to defend the population, which was at that time under the KLA control, and for the KLA to defend itself from the attacks at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm afraid there's something missing from this picture for me. I mean, I understand we have other evidence about this, but so far as this witness's presentation of evidence isn't concerned, this doesn't bear any relationship to reality. That may not be your purpose, but it's not clear to me what they're defending if the population want to stay where they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just the transcript, a technical problem. Line 5, in paragraph -- page 21, line 5, the word "around" appears there and what he said was "order," "and in your order, you say," and that could be important in a future reading of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, what you have described, the period you have described from the 24th, when the NATO bombing started, and up until the 1st of April, would it be a correct description of those events to say that you were -- the KLA was withdrawing from the area it had been holding on the 24th?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This is the period when the KLA was retreating because of the Serb forces who were attacking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand you're in control -- you claim to be in control of territory from which you're retreating, but the impression I have at the moment is perhaps the population were in the way. What was happening to the population that required you to have them moved? I can't lead you on this. I want to know what you're -- we have other evidence in this, but I want to know what your evidence is about what was happening in Bellanice and that area which gave rise to the order, you say, to leave it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order was issued before all this happened in zones B and C. The order was for the population to leave the Bellanice area because other villages were evacuated earlier for security reasons. These villages were formerly under the KLA control, because there was fighting here between the Serb forces and them. So it was a question of safety for the population. While the population from Bellanice did not relocate, they remained there -- most of the population remained in Bellanice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was just noticing that the witness was pointing on his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it's not on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And not on the ELMO but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- on the screen. That's why I was standing up. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be that I missed the date of the order, then. I assumed it was about the 31st of March or the 1st of April. Has the order a different date?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, the order bears the date of the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm now more confused, then, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When this order was issued on the 1st of April, were -- when you issued this order on the 1st of April, was the KLA line of defence north or south of Bellanice?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the order was issued -- as I said on the 31st, the forces started to withdraw from zone B, together with the population. When I issued the order, this line here was not there. I wrote it at midnight. The order was for the 123rd, 124th, and 125th Brigade to withdraw and go to this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But when you issued the order, was the civilian population behind the KLA line? Basically, were they still in the area held by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the KLA-held zone, and the order says, after 12.00, after midnight. It's an order for the withdrawal of the 123rd, 124th, and 125th Brigade, and also the withdrawal of the population from these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I know it's time for a break, I think. Am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. The break will be at 10 minutes to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay, good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zyrapi, when, in the execution -- in the execution of -- when your order was being executed, were the forces referred to in your order to withdraw through the area of Bellanice and up northwards to establish the line between B and C? Is that a correct understanding of the situation?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a correct understanding. The units that I mentioned had to withdraw from zone B, withdraw through the territory of Bellanice, because the Serbs were attacking from Gajrak and Banja and then also from Blace. So the territory through which they could withdraw narrowed quite a lot. That's why they had to withdraw in the territory -- through the territory of Bellanice and establish themselves in this line that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So when you earlier said that you ordered the withdrawal of the population for safety reasons -- I'm not sure how I can do this without leading. When you ordered the population to withdraw for safety reasons, did that have to do with the movement of KLA forces and the front line?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was for the population to move alongside the withdrawal or the movement of the front line of the KLA - it's parallel - so that the population would not be at the front line where these units were at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is the picture still very confused, or should I -- is it clearer now what the situation is? I can try to explore it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was ordered and what the witness wanted to do is clear, but why it was done remains unclear. But you may be relying on other evidence for that, so we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, why did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I find it very difficult at the moment to understand how keeping the population, in the large numbers we've heard about, behind the KLA line was going to protect them, but that's -- and that's my difficulty, if I can spell it out for you. It's not clear to me what this witness thought was happening to them that gave rise to the need for them to move, or would happen to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, in your experience as a military officer, when you have a moving front line, is it normal procedure to order the civilian population away from the front line?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially when we speak about the type of combat that was carried out in Kosova, it was normal for us to order the movement of the population but also of the KLA, because the Serbian forces were attacking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is it normal procedure to order the civilian population out of an area where there's combat?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not normal procedure, a regular procedure, but keeping in mind the developments at the time, we issued the order for the population to move because they were at risk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What were they at risk from? What caused a risk to them?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there could be fighting between the forces; there could be use of heavy weaponry, not only light weaponry. So that could cause the death of civilians during that time, especially in the territories where the KLA was in control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, let's try to move the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: By all means, move on, but that answer, if it's been translated accurately, suggests that you increase the risk by keeping the population in the area where the KLA are in control, unless I've, again, misunderstood what's being said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Excuse me. We still do need the upper part of the map before ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, while we move the map, where did you move the population to go -- where was the population supposed to go?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the order, the population was to withdraw towards the village of Ngucat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My apologies. Excuse me -- yes.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So towards the village of Ngucat and the Berisha mountains, because they could be sheltered there and they would be safer there, in this territory. This is a small map and you cannot see all the details, but the Berisha mountains are here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you point again to the Berisha mountains, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So what would be the distance from the newly established front line to the area where the civilians --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's important, when you asked him to point again to the Berisha mountains, that the record show that he pointed to the area around the letter C on the map, so that the record will show where he was indicating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The official record will be the video and that's my reason for not doing that, as I would normally do in a domestic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But you may be right where there may be occasions where it's important to do this. I think we would be here forever in relation to this witness if he had to do this every time he pointed to something on the map. It will be available to you to see in due course if you need it. This is one section -- a section like this of the video would be made available, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand, but for appeal purposes, we rarely work from video and we always work from transcripts. I don't recall ever seeing a video of a trial session during an appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. For the avoidance of doubt, Mr. Zyrapi, would you point again to the Berisha mountains.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Berisha mountains start here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you're pointing generally to an area which is below C and it's roughly to the right of the map from Ngucat and above, is that Temeqin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Temeqin is on my right, here. I'm pointing at it. I'm pointing to the Temeqin village, and this is Ngucat village. So the Berisha mountains, this whole area is the Berisha mountains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're pointing now as far up as Kerzharek. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, the civilian population that -- was any part of the civilian part of the population moved into the area C?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you indicate with a pointer there where, in the area C, they were located.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, this is a small-scale map and I cannot be very precise, but they were located here from Ngucat village, between Ngucat and Javor, in the direction of the passes here, towards Divjake --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the whole territory here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. So the area that has been indicated is just below the C and to the eastern part of the C.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also, to the east, this part that I already mentioned, because this is a flat area but there are other parts deep there between Divjake and Kroimire. There are some passes there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the distance between the KLA front line and the location of the civilians?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The front line was here, while the population was behind the front line, about 500 metres away. Even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But is it -- no. Well, let's move to the other area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If the usher would be kind enough to move the map so we can see the area indicated with E, F, G. Let's pull it a little further down, like the top -- sorry. Other direction. Yes. I think that's -- that's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, you've already indicated that when the NATO bombing started, the KLA in this part of Kosovo held the areas E, F, and G. When did the KLA forces reach the area F?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the attacks started, part of the population - I don't know the exact date now; it's on the 25th or the 26th - part of the population in this zone withdrew and went to the area marked with F.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, it was one or two days after the attacks had started.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you present in this area yourself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I wasn't personally present in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So how do you know that this was the position of the KLA forces in this area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the reports that were submitted by zone commanders at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then when did the KLA forces move out of the area and establish the line between F and G?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the reports of zone commanders, the Serb forces penetrated this area very quickly, in a matter of three or four hours. And from these reports, since I was not personally present, I know that on that day, part of the population and of the forces withdrew in the F and G areas. Part of the population and forces withdrew also in this direction, in the direction of the area marked with C.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So when had the withdrawal to the area G been completed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, because I wasn't personally present, but according to the reports, until the end of March. So the KLA forces and the population from this area moved to this area by the end of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if I could ask the usher just to move the map down again so we can see the area D.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, the area indicated by a D, did the KLA remain in this area or did you also move out of that area after the NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the beginning of NATO bombing, the KLA forces remained here until -- well, when the intensity of attacks lowered in area C, I went two or three days earlier - I don't remember exactly - to the D area. I visited this area to see how the situation was. In this area, the population and the KLA stayed, remained there, for some time, even after I left, but I don't know exactly how long they remained in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I have one exhibit, but we can do that maybe after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will have to break now, Mr. Zyrapi, for 20 minutes. Could you please go with the usher. He'll show you again where to wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we will resume at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we see Exhibit P2462, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, do you recognise the document that you have on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you provide this document to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where did you get that document from?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the archives of the 125th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you collect the document there yourself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, would you please read the title of this document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's "Kosovo Liberation Army, Pastrik Operational Zone, 125th Brigade." Below, it's written: "Report on the Gruesome Tragedy of Serb Offensives in Medevce Village, Prizren Municipality." And it continues. It reads: "As all over Kosovo ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I object to him reading from this document. I don't think Your Honours will appreciate the objection, quite frankly, until you see the English version, which I would ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's in front of me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can have it on the other screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not asking -- actually, I don't need the witness to read from the document. I will ask the witness to maybe -- sorry, there's more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Our essential objection, Your Honours, is that this is polemic, is what it is. It's not a first-hand account. It's a second- or third-hand account. Unless I'm missing a point, the village of Medevce is not even charged in the indictment. The report is in June of 1989, and supposedly there was a prior report, which is not being introduced into evidence, which would be more accurate, if, under these circumstances, anything could be accurate, dated April 12, 1999. That's on the last page of the document. There's a number of reasons, Your Honour, why this should not come into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to get from the witness who had signed the report and what his familiarity with the report is, and then I was, indeed, going to request its admission. It is a summary report, as I understand it, of events that occurred in the zone of responsibility of this commander, summing up the period from the beginning of the NATO bombing until June 1999. We submit it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's find out from the witness, through your questions, what this document is, who compiled it, and the likely sources of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we go to the last page of this document, please, and could we zoom in on the signature block. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, can you see who have -- who has signed the document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an officer who was in the 125th Brigade. His name is Hasan Morina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Before testifying today, did you read the report?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the purpose that you seek to achieve by referring to this, Mr. Marcussen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the witness what he knows about how the document has been compile -- how it has been drafted up, what it is, the contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm allow you to at least go that far to establish its authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, from your reading of the document, how has this document been compiled, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see, this document is a report that covers the time from the beginning of the NATO air-strikes up until April and May. It is written by the officer who was in that zone and it pertains to the happenings in that relevant territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So am I correct that what you're saying is that the report concerns the area in which this officer was operating and within his zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report by an officer who was operating within his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now I ask you the question I asked a moment ago,

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What is it you seek to achieve by referring to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We submit this puts in context the events in several of our crime sites, but in the area where some of our crimes were committed, and this puts in context what was happening at the time that all crimes were -- the crime sites in the indictment were being committed, Mala Krusa, this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we go back to the first page again, please. Mr. Sepenuk, the document does contain reference to the area that we've been concerned about. I note the point you make about the particular so-called tragedy which is not in the indictment and therefore will be of no significance. But there are parts of the document which do relate to the area, and we're told by the witness it's compiled by an officer who was active in the area at the time within his own zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: But, of course, Your Honour, the reference to Medevce experiencing three offences, that's, as I understand it, not part of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, that's the point I'm making. But it does refer to the movement of population to Mamusa, and it also refers to the offensive that the witness has been telling us about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours would find it helpful, then I would withdraw my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it may be. But we are conscious of the need to distinguish the parts of it that are relevant from the parts of it that are irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we see the second page again, please. Is there a problem with showing the second page? And then the final page, please, if the third one is, indeed, the final. Yes, carry on, Mr. Marcussen. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that actually completes -- if this document is admitted, that completes the Prosecution's direct examination of the witness. I would note that we have received very late notice of a number of documents that are going to be used in cross-examination of this witness. As a matter of fact, just an hour before, even while the session has been going on, we've been notified of a number of documents the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, I think I would hold my fire on that, if I were you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I just wanted to indicate to the Defence that we are not, on this particular occasion, going to object to the use of these documents. We have been discussing this. So this is why I'm just taking this opportunity to indicate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The documents that the witness has been referring to so far, when were they first notified to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Some in the witness notification and some in a supplemental information sheet that was sent to the Defence last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you say "witness notification," do you mean the original 65 ter list of witnesses and exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It was also in the 65 ter filing, but then we filed these weekly. On Thursdays, I think, we file a witness notification indicating the exhibits that are going to be used. The exhibits that were included there were exhibits -- Exhibits P2447 through P2453, and then by a supplemental information sheet, we indicated that we were also going to use P2457 through P2468. The original witness notification also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, my notice, P2469, and that was intimated on the 31st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The order will be, first, counsel for General Ojdanic and then we'll follow the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What about the motion requesting assistance and guidance? Is that now redundant, as I was hoping it might be? Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we kind of have a consensus about how to do this. Even though I've requested guidance from the Chamber, I'm going to make a suggestion to you. There are a number of documents that are in Albanian and have not been translated and they're in the process of being translated by CLSS, and my guess is that's about a two-week process to get that accomplished. I tried to find somebody that could give me just some sense, at least, of what they contained beyond the bare indication from the Prosecution and failed in that regard, so we've asked CLSS to translate them for us. The second thing is that there's an 84-page document provided under Rule 68 that is in B/C/S that is not translated, has been sent to CLSS, is in the process of being translated, and what I'm told about its contents, it appears to be perhaps quite significant in terms of cross-examining this witness, and it would be important for Your Honours to be able to see the translation for that cross-examination to make sense, I would think. And the third thing is a rather short, I think, six-page Albanian statement of a witness that was provided as Rule 68 material with regard to this witness. What I'm suggesting, Your Honour, that we do is this: That we go forward with cross-examination now and try to complete cross-examination of this witness, and then once we get those translations, if we can make the case to you that there is information in there important enough to justify bringing him back, then you get to make that decision and decide whether to bring him back or not. And I think that's probably the logical way to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we're extremely grateful for that positive approach --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- and welcome it. So Mr. Visnjic -- no. Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, just before you start, Judge Chowhan does have a question he would like to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to have intruded while you were standing, and thank you for allowing me this. Now, you've given us the details about the administrative structure of this organisation you were talking of, dealing at length, and the various echelons it had in its working system, the way it was commanded, the way it was ordered, and all of that, but it would be functioning only when it had funds. Nothing has been stated as to the funds and how this part of the organisation was being conducted and who was giving the salaries and who was receiving it and what was your salary, while being there, so on and so forth. This question did arise. Because for an organisation as huge as you've depicted really needs a good deal of money, and that is what I thought I should request you to apprise us with. And I'm thankful for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, to my knowledge, the funding of the KLA was from Vendluadja Therret, the Fatherland Calling Fund, which was based in the diaspora, and also from funds raised from voluntary donations inside Kosova. These funds were dedicated to the development and functioning of the KLA. These are the two funds that were used for the KLA. As far as salaries are concerned, starting from me and to the lowest-level soldier, nobody received salaries. Nobody was paid. The KLA was a voluntary army. To the very end, we fought without any payment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Zyrapi, I'm Norman Sepenuk, and I'm an attorney for General Ojdanic. Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'm going to start with your testimony yesterday, and, in fact, I'd like to start in early March of 1998, where you talked about the attack on the Jashari family, marking the beginning of the conflict between the Serbian forces and the KLA. And that refers to the March 2nd fire-fight between Adem Jashari, who, I think it's fair to say, was a KLA hero, and his family and Serb forces, ending with the deaths of Mr. Jashari and a number of members of his family. And you, I take it, regard that as the beginning of the conflict between Serb forces and the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I take it as the beginning of the conflict, and this is what I stated in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. And then just a few months after that, in May of 1998, May 28th, 1998, you entered Kosovo as a KLA member; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And at that time, as you also said yesterday, from the point of view of the KLA, the KLA was not at the required level of development and organisation. Both at the local staff level and the general level, it was not well organised. It was more of a guerrilla organisation than a regular army. Those are your feelings; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I've already stated in my statement, the KLA army at that time was a guerrilla force, and it consisted of voluntary soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. And despite the fact that it was a guerrilla army, though, is it fair to say - and we've had testimony at this trial, and I'll ask you, Mr. Zyrapi, if you agree with it - that by mid-July of 1998, the KLA held up to 50 per cent of the territory of Kosovo, including three of the four main access roads? Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact percentage, but more or less it is an exact statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. But you, Mr. Zyrapi, and others, your colleagues, recognise that to reach your ultimate goal of controlling Kosovo or maybe, to put it in your terms, to reach your ultimate goal of liberating Kosovo, you needed more than a popular guerrilla army. Isn't that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You needed a stronger army.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, stronger and more organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. And your colleague Ramush Haradinaj, I think it's fair to say, agreed with you, because you shared with us yesterday the Prosecution Exhibit 2453, which was the work meeting of the Dukagjin upper level concerning organising that zone. Dukagjin was one of the seven zones in the KLA at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And this document, Prosecution Exhibit 2453, states - and, again, this is the meeting where Mr. Haradinaj was there and a number of his high-ranking assistants - and Mr. Haradinaj, who is called Smajli, states, in the first page, "Underground activity has yielded its results." And that, I take it, refers to the success that the KLA had reached by that point. That's a question.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, his success that he achieved through combat at that time has made him deserve the level that he was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right. And he says, or at least the document says: "This war today belongs to the entire people, not to one group. It's about the liberation of the country through a general insurgency. Knowing the requirements of the war of an area which is of geostrategic significance, our war must be extended. We need to have a regular army." And I think it's fair to say you felt the same way, did you not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and we worked in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. And, as you said yesterday, this document refers to the whole notion of unity of command in the operative zone of Dukagjin. In the document, on page 6, the statement is made: "The formation of the operational staff of the plain of Dukagjin was agreed and proclaimed unanimously," and then the document goes on to say: "It was decided by a majority that the commander of the operational staff of the plain of Dukagjin should be Smajli," which is Ramush Haradinaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And in this document, on page 7, Mr. Haradinaj says: "The central staff has not been giving us the instructions we require. It has been absent." And Mustafa, who was one of his assistants, as I understand it, says: "We are attempting to construct --" excuse me, says: "If we do not create a regular army, we cannot be victorious. I am in favour of Smajli." So the general consensus at that meeting was that the zone had to be organised, Mr. Haradinaj was the head of the zone, and they were in favour of proceeding with -- in a more organised fashion so that the army and their zone could become stronger. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how you can interpret this. As for what you mentioned about the staff, to what level it was involved, that I don't know for that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. So continuing with the chronology. In July, the Serb offensive started against all the territories, as you testified yesterday, where the KLA was in control, and this was essentially the beginning of the Serb summer offensive to regain control of the lost territories; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And you continued yesterday by saying that the general situation in August and September could be described as fighting in the area where the KLA was in control; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And September and October were a continuation of the fighting that started in August and even earlier.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is according to the information I received, because during September and October, I was not in Kosova at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I understand. And is it fair to say that by the end of October, roughly, the end of October, 1998, Serb forces had recaptured most of the territory previously controlled by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And then at the end of October, 1998, as I'm sure you recall, we had what's called in shorthand the Holbrooke-Milosevic cease-fire; it's also the Clark-Naumann-Milosevic cease-fire, pursuant to Security Council Resolution 1199. But the short of it is, there was a cease-fire and the Serbian forces pull back their troops, both army and police, to pre -- to the earlier levels. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And during the time immediately after that, late October and then November and December, is it fair to say that the KLA used this time to regroup and consolidate your forces?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That time was used to consolidate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And you became Chief of Staff, Chief of the General Staff, in November, 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And by the way -- thank you. And I've yet to see an exact date. Do you know the exact date you became the Chief of Staff of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date. It was sometime in the second half of November, but, as I said, I can't give you an exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the end of December, 1998, you summarise, sort of, the year-end state of the KLA in a document introduced by the Prosecution, Prosecution Exhibit 2460, which was the operative directorate composed of the written statements, based on the written statements, of the operative zone commanders of Dukagjin, Pastrik, Nerodimlje, Sala, and Llap. Do you recall that testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a report. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. And you mentioned in your testimony that you received this document from the General Staff archives; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Where are those archives?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The archives of the General Staff of the KLA, part of them were collected by the TMK, and then they were sent to the central archives of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right, but -- and thank you for that. But my question is: Where are these archives? Where? What city? What village? Where are they located? Where the archives located?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The archives of the General Staff are in Prishtina, where the staff of the TMK - in English, Kosova Protection Corps - is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And how long have they been at that location, the archives?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents were lodged there immediately after the war, while some of the documents were sent later on to the central archives of Kosova, which is still in Prishtina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: This Prosecution Exhibit 2460, that shows a copy going to the archive. So after this document was generated, did a copy immediately go to the archive?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every document that was written was archived both at the staff and in the zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And it also notes, by the way, that it had a seal. Did the General Staff have a seal?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And when did the General Staff acquire a seal, at what point; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The seal was obtained later. It was by November or December.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
