utterances.text: Okay. And when it was archived -- you say this document, for example, was immediately archived. Where at that time was it archived? Where was it archived on December 28, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was archived immediately with the staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- where we were operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And where was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, it was in Divjake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Which is where? Enlighten me on that, please.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the village of Divjake. It's located in the Berisha mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And how did you happen to choose this document to bring to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document that I brought here as an example of disciplinary measures taken by the KLA, disciplinary measures against the soldiers or officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Sir, actually we're talking about a different document now, so let's be clear about it. I'm talking now about the document, Prosecution Exhibit 2460, which is a report on statements. It's your year-end summary of what's happening in the Kosovo Liberation Army. Do you remember that document? You testified about it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document that was written at the end of the year was written on the 28th of December, and it was a report based on the reports coming from the zones, written reports from the zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I appreciate that, and I'm going to ask you some questions about that in just a few minutes. But I'm just asking, sir, how you happened to choose this document to bring to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the first document that was submitted in written form. This was the first one written.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Had you had a conversation with Mr. Marcussen or any other member of the Prosecution's office or any investigator with the Prosecution as to the existence of the archives? In other words, before you came here, did you acquaint the Prosecutor's office with the fact that there were archives for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I made the statement, I also said that there were archives of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. But did you have a discussion about that with the Prosecutor's office before you came here?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You told him about that when you gave your statement? You gave two statements, one in October, 2005, and one in January, 2006. Is it your testimony that at those times you advised the Prosecutors, or the representative of the Prosecutors, that there was such a thing called the KLA archives?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement I gave in July, I think I mentioned there that there is an archive of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. And at that time did any member of the Prosecution's office request the opportunity to see what was in the archives, to examine what was in it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave the statement in July where I said that there are such archives, I was here in The Hague, not in Prishtina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. But when you told whoever it was -- do you remember who you told that to when you gave your statement in January, 2006? Do you recall who you told that to in July of 2006?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not give a statement in January, 2006; it was July, 2006. And I said what I said about the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. And did the person that you gave the statement to, or any other member of the Prosecutor's office, ever follow up on that and say, "We'd like to see the archives. We'd like to visit there. We'd like to see what's in it"? Did you ever get any kind of inquiry like that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I submitted the documents that I got from the archives to the Prosecution office in Prishtina, and they sent the documents here. I was not approached directly from anyone to say that they wanted to have a look at those archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And is this document, 2460, which is the December 28th, 1998 document, is that one of the documents you gave to the Prosecutor's office in Prishtina to send here?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document was given to them, and it was sent here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And when did you give this document to them? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember, but it was before I came here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Was it in the last few weeks?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the last few weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And so I take it, is the archives generally open? For example, if one of the members of the Defence team was to make an inquiry, could they have access to these archives, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who has the right to have access to the archives. It's their inner problem, their inner administrative issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And based on your knowledge of the archives and the fact you were Chief of the General Staff of the KLA, if we wanted, if one of the Defence people, one of the Defence lawyers or one of the defendants wanted to have access to the archives, who would be the person to talk to about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have to go to the place where the archives are, both to the staff and also to the Kosova archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not sure that this is really cross-examination. It sounds more to me like an exploration as to how the Defence might get access to documents, which we could make the witness available to discuss those issues, maybe, outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Your Honour, not in the least. We've already received -- excuse me, Your Honour. I didn't mean to interrupt if you were going to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On you go, Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes. We've already received, very recently, Rule 68 material, and, my goodness, is it Mr. Marcussen's position -- and I'll ask this: I take it the Prosecution's office has never made an inquiry from the archives? I mean, there could be all sorts of material in those archives. It could be very useful. In this case, my understanding is that the Prosecution has never even inquired about it until Mr. Zyrapi, the witness, voluntarily furnished some evidence a few weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I personally don't see a problem with the cross-examination on these lines. We're all agreed that it's perfectly appropriate to follow this line, and we will repel the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So maybe just one or two more questions on this, Mr. Zyrapi. As precisely as you can, please tell us the person or persons who should be contacted with respect to obtaining records from the KLA archives.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Kosova archives has a director; I don't know his name. And as regards the archives at the staff, you can approach the commander there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And that is? Who is that person?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the KPC staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now the commander of the KPC staff is Sulejman Selimi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Zyrapi. Now, I'd like to just get to a discussion of this document; that's the document of December 28, 1998. It's a year-end summary of the situation in the KLA, and, of course, it's signed by you, as the Chief of Staff, and based on the reports of your zone commanders, at least five of the zones. By the way, what about the other two zones? As I read this, the other two zones did not submit reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two zones were not included because they did not submit a written report. They gave an oral report and then followed up with a written one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we'll start with "Leading and Commanding," first page, and it says: "It can be stated that they are at an appropriate level in all operating zones." And then you go on to say, or at least the report goes on to say: "There is a considerable lack of professional staff, especially in the Dukagjin and Nerodimlje operating zones." Now, do you recall whether steps were taken to improve that situation that you noted?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember there were also requests for sending personnel to this area. We sent officers there in order to complete the staff of the operative zone, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And the whole point of this was to make the Kosovo Liberation Army a stronger, more effective army; isn't that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that, to strengthen the KLA both in leadership and command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. And in that same paragraph, "Leading and Commanding," you state -- or it is stated that: "In most of the command positions of all the zones mentioned, at all command levels from the squad to the operating zone level, people have proved themselves in combat up to now, both in terms of bravery and organisational, and command skills have been appointed." And I take it that was a matter of some pride to you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were people who had some experience, and we wanted to raise the level of leadership and command at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. And then, going to part B, it's called "Combat Morale," and it says: "With the reorganisation and the filling of vacancies with staff, with reappointments that have been carried out in all operating zones, combat morale of the soldiers and the population that is joining the KLA more and more by the day has risen considerably. In all the zones, great interest is felt, especially by the young [Realtime transcript read in error 'junk'], to join the KLA." Did you find at this time and the months prior to this time that there was a lot of enthusiasm, particularly among young men, to join the KLA? And were you trying to take advantage of that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The transcript again. At 51, 13, it says "junk" and it's "young," I think the witness said "young".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's one that I imagine would be sorted out in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's very important to draw significant ones to our attention. Where it's "no" and the answer was "yes," then it's important to identify it. But where it looks as though it may be ironed out later by the checking exercise, it's not so necessary to do so. But please don't hesitate. If you are in doubt, raise the matter. Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And you go on to state: "High combat morale has been shown in clashes that KLA units had with enemy police, paramilitary/military forces in different parts of Kosovo, especially in the Dukagjin, Pastrik, and Llap operating zones. The enemy suffered considerable losses in dead and equipment with minimal consequences for our KLA units." And, again, a matter which, I take it, was a source of satisfaction for you.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a report that was sent by the operative zones, and then a summary was made of all the reports and sent to the deputy commander of the General Staff. So these were the experiences of the soldiers of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And on the next page, it talks about training. Again, this is the situation as of December 28, 1998, and it says: "More work should be done with new soldiers that join the KLA in all operative zones in the following segments," and it mentions "knowledge of the collective armament, knowledge of the tactical actions, military rules in general." Do you recall whether you did work on those areas after that, January, February, March? Did you work on those areas?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we worked on all these areas, training, personnel, from simple soldiers to the commanding levels, commanding levels at the squad level and up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And the reason you did that, I assume, is a very simple one, and that is that you wanted to improve the Kosovo Liberation Army and not be satisfied with the status quo. You wanted to keep getting better and stronger. Isn't that fair?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We also had a statute, and we worked in the direction of training our personnel. We wanted to be ready. We didn't know what would happen after the status quo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. So you wanted to be ready and continue to be prepared for any situation that would arise.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. And then in item D, "Mobilisation and Matters of Personnel," you state, or the report states, that: "Mobilisation in all operative zones has been carried out on a voluntary basis which will continue also in the future. Up until now, the level of mobilisation has been high." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember mobilisation was carried out on a voluntary basis and it continued like that even later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right. And then further down in that paragraph is something which struck me, anyway - and I don't think we should go into the incident in any kind of detail - but apparently some young KLA members were killed in a fire-fight, the thrust of this being that they were killed because they didn't have the training and the discipline to handle the situation. Is that, sort of, a shorthand summary of what happened?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a summary of what happened. During the summer offensive, there were soldiers who were not trained and had no military experience, and they were killed in the fighting because they were not prepared, well prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And I'm sure it's fair to say that, as Chief of the General Staff, you wanted to make sure that nothing like that ever happened again.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why we took steps to conduct training.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So that people who were members of the Kosovo Liberation Army, even the very -- younger members, could obtain the training and discipline to be effective fighters. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Then we turn to "Logistics," which is item E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sepenuk, I understand the nature of this cross-examination. It's one with which I'm much more familiar when dealing with a jury, this emphasis of the strength of your position taken from things which are in this document. But remember, please, that a balance has to be struck here, and, no doubt, you've got that in mind. And remember also, please, that we are able to read this document and you can be sure it will be carefully read.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you know, without -- I don't want to say too much, Your Honour, but our point here is to -- well, I'm not going to get into our point. But thank you for your comments, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I also think, in case you were in any doubt, that you're clearly pushing at an open door with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, your going to simply get confirmation of everything in that report in response to every question you ask. That's just the nature of the way in which this evidence is being presented by the witness, and we are alert to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. Well, I might as well say it, Your Honour. We're trying to show that great efforts were made to make this a stronger, more effective army, a more formidable army, that these six men sitting behind me had reason to be very afraid of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that message has already been clearly presented through this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. Let me just move on, then, to the combat situation, because I think we can add something to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Where it says "Combat Situation, Enemy Forces," and that's paragraph G, where it says that: "Following UN Security Council Resolution 1199, enemy forces have withdrawn from some dominant points. For example, Sukat and the Dukagjin Operative Zone, and some of them have not been placed under the control of our forces." I don't know whether that's -- is that a typographical error? Should that be "and some of them have been placed" or "some of them have not been placed." The English translation says: "Some of them have not been placed under the control of our forces." So I'm simply asking you, Mr. Zyrapi, whether you can help us on that. First of all, let me ask you: You recall that -- it says: "Enemy forces have withdrawn from some dominant points." That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And maybe --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and the report is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And maybe I can clear it up with the part under "Our Forces," and that says: "The increase in the number of soldiers is noticeable, especially in the Dukagjin Operative Zone. Following the enemy offensive, the repositioning of forces has been carried out in all operative zones, and we can freely say that the territory controlled by our units is now of a greater percentage than prior to the enemy offensive." Is that what happened; the short of it being the Serb forces pulled out and the KLA forces moved back in?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to the reports that were sent by zone commanders, it is evident that the Serb forces withdrew after this resolution. However, the installment of KLA was not in large territories. It was narrowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: But you did fill in a number of positions, did you not, Mr. Zyrapi? When I say "you," the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A number of positions we did fill in, but not all of the positions. According to the agreement, we were supposed to stay away from the roads, 2 to 3 kilometres away from the roads. Therefore, we were not able to cover all the positions, all the points, that had previously been under KLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And I'll ask you one final question from this document, and that is, it says: "Proposals for the use of tactical and operational units for combat activities in the future," and you set forth a number of items here, "acting in commando groups in towns and inside the zones where the enemy is active, cutting out enemy supply lines through diversion actions, hitting everywhere the living enemy forces in order to inflict insecurity at all times and everywhere." Those are traditional guerrilla tactics, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are traditional guerrilla tactics which are followed by certain regular armies as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Right. So, in other words, you were trying to have the advantages of a stronger, regular army combined with, when necessary, the use of hit-and-run guerrilla tactics, when the situation called for that. Is that fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And then continuing our narrative, the record shows that, during January and February and March, despite the cease-fire, the KLA continued its fight against Serb forces primarily by ambushes. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the report, but there are reports --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which clearly show that --

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: When you say "can't see the report," I haven't shown you anything. We're through now with your December 1998 report. I'm going on to another subject and I'm saying, during January, February and March of 1999, there were clashes back and forth with Serb forces; and even though there was a cease-fire, the KLA did continue its attacking forays, a good part of which were by ambush. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct, as far as January and February are concerned. What I said yesterday referred to these defensive attacks. These attacks were more defensive in nature than attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll just go into a couple of those to illustrate a point, one way or the other. But I do have an assessment from the Kosovo Verification Mission, and it's an assessment of January 2nd, 1999. This is just a few days after your December 28, 1998 report. It's Defence Exhibit 3D0359, and it's the last page of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't know if the exhibit number is correct, but I don't think there is such an exhibit in e-court. And we were notified of a document, 3D356, and the next one was 352. But maybe it's a mistake just in the citing of the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is -- heads will roll, Your Honour. I'm sorry, but the number I have is 359. But let me tell you, it's the KVM Blue Book for January 2nd, 1999. I don't think there's -- of course, it's going to be in the English anyway, Your Honour, and if it wouldn't offend the Trial Chamber, perhaps if I could just read from it, because he's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please do that and let's keep our fingers crossed that it may appear yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Here is what this assessment says, Mr. Zyrapi. This is an assessment by the Kosovo Verification Mission; that's the OSCE Kosovo Verification Commission. See if you agree with this: "There are indications the KLA may be coming more closely unified under a centralised command structure. Units of the KLA are now being identified to KVM patrols by specific unit designation. Areas of responsibility are being adjusted by the KLA, and loosely affiliated groups may be coming under centralised control." And I'm assuming that you agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard those statements. The organisation continued to the extent that it covered every unit that operated in the territory of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. And the report goes on to say: "An interesting trend is developing with the VJ becoming more cooperative with OSCE and its operation and the KLA becoming more belligerent and uncooperative at their security positions." Do you agree with that statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I remember, that entire period, January and February and even December, I know that there was cooperation. The OSCE came to check and had contacts with the KLA. And I don't think that there was lack of cooperation in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So you certainly don't agree with that statement, then; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to take another crack at an exhibit, Your Honour, Defence Exhibit 3D363. And this is from the so-called Blue Book, January 9th Blue Book, of the Kosovo Verification Mission, and it is numbered incident number 2. If the usher would put that up on the screen. I think you have to just click on 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think it's the fourth page of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's the fourth page. Thank you, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And here's the report of the KVM. It says that: "RC 1 reported that prior to 1040 hours, a MUP patrol, consisting of one Lada Niva and two Pinzgauers, were ambushed 4 kilometres north-east of Suva Reka vicinity, DM," and then a number. "The patrol was fired on from well-constructed, well-camouflaged trenches which appeared to have been occupied for several days. The following casualties were reported: 3 MUP killed in action, 3 MUP wounded in action, and 3 Albanian civilians were wounded who happened to drive into the ambush accidentally. The KLA departed the area immediately following the ambush. An examination of the trenches revealed 7.62-millimetre and 12.7-millimetre shell casings. RPG rounds were also fired. The MUPs apparently died while still inside the Pinzgauers." Now, do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember this incident, and I don't remember either the date or the place where it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Assuming the incident occurred, as it sets forth here, under then current -- under then existing KLA rules and regulations, would you have been the person who ordered that ambush?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, that the operations would be approved by the General Staff. For this particular incident, I don't remember the date and the place where it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: But, again, assuming that it did occur, as stated here, would you have been the person to authorise that attack?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The zone commander also had the authority to carry out these operations, but the operations had to be approved by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the date of this incident, Mr. Sepenuk?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: It's the 8th of January, 1999, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this report from a minute after midnight until the following midnight? I'm trying to understand the part at the top where the 8 is, so that I can understand any future ones you refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But it looks like 801 up until 824.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And in the latter part of that document - and I believe it's page 11 - here's what the Kosovo Verification Mission says about that attack, Mr. Zyrapi. It says: "The well-executed ambush against a MUP patrol near Suva Reka indicates good training and planning, and validates the KLA's earlier threats to retaliate against MUP/VJ patrols and check-points. It appears that the KLA does not acknowledge the cease-fire any more and will most likely strike again using the same tactics." Is that a fair statement? Did the KLA have any intention of abiding by that cease-fire that took place at the end of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The intention was to respect the cease-fire agreement that was signed in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Then what would the point of that ambush have been? Why was that ambush authorised? Wasn't that a violation of the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned yesterday and today, when talking about these small-scale attacks on the part of the KLA, that is attacking check-points of the Serb forces, that constituted an obstacle for the KLA, the movement of the KLA units from one territory to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And that's the way you viewed it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this particular incident. I can see the date. It is mentioned in the report, but it does not mention the location where it occurred. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on to another document. It's 3D374.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. I had lost track of the time there, Mr. Sepenuk. I think we should break now and move on to that document after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Again we have to break, Mr. Zyrapi. Could you go with the usher, leave the court with him, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will resume at 6.00, and we will sit until about 10 past 7.00 or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Either, Mr. Sepenuk, the exhibit is wrongly numbered or we're disappointed not to see it on the screen. We're still on the last one, I think. You wanted 3D374, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I believe I asked him about that, and I'm prepared to go on to another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought that was the one you were about to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you were interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I don't think so. And by the way, this might be an appropriate time to bring it up. The Defence is a little bit concerned about time in terms of -- I don't really have that much more, Your Honour, and -- but we want to make sure we don't exceed -- I take it, will there be the usual ruling or will there be extra time for this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I was concerned when I saw the line you were following; that's why I intervened earlier. And the Prosecution took just over 4.5 hours in chief, so I was hoping that that would be the guideline for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Well, I -- personally I don't have that much more left, Your Honour. I'll certainly keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's carry on and see how we get on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I'm just going to ask you, we're in the period now -- we started with -- we're in the period now January/February/March of 1999, the period leading up to the war, and I'm just going to ask you a few more questions about some incidents that happened during that period, and I'd like the ushers to put up 3D362. Again, this is another Kosovo Verification Mission document for the period 5 March 1999. And if we can go to -- I believe it's page 9. It's incident number 8. Yes. And according to this report, Mr. Zyrapi, at 1000 hours -- it has to do with a KLA ambush of a MUP convoy, and it says: "At 1000 hours, a MUP convoy was ambushed by approximately 15 to 20 KLA at," and it gives coordinate. "The attack occurred while the MUP were rotating their personnel and delivering food. The KLA fired two RPG 7 rounds followed by machine-gun fire wounding 11 MUP, 6 seriously." Now, first of all, in 5 March 1999, is this again an attack that you personally would have ordered or approved?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it required approval from us, of course we would have approved it, but I don't remember this incident and the place where it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that assuming what the KVM says here is true that the MUP were rotating their personnel and delivering food, is it your position that what happened here was not a violation of the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And that is because?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say earlier, yesterday and today, there were attacks on check-points. I don't remember this specific incident. It mentions the territory where the attack took place but not the exact location. It should be in the reports that contain the dates of this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: If the -- I'd like to put up another exhibit, 3D179.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. Zyrapi, this is an OSCE, Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, KVM, Kosovo Verification Mission, background report on compliance by the parties in Kosovo between the end of the Rambouillet talks and the beginning of the second Paris talks. It's 23rd February to 11 March 1999. That's the period covered. And in the opening paragraph it states: "Unprovoked attacks by the KLA against the police have continued and the number of casualties sustained by the security forces has increased." Does that -- does that refresh your recollection as to what was happening during that period? Were you as the Chief of the General Staff of the KLA approving increased attacks against the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, during this period of time there were attacks but not increased attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right. And the report goes on to cite a number of these attacks. I'm not going to mention them all. I'll mention a few. On page 2 it says: "On 27 February, a police patrol was ambushed west of Pristina airfield with one police officer killed and one wounded apparently by KLA sniper fire." Do you have any recollection of that at all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Another -- in another part of the report it says: "Three police officers were wounded and one of them later died in a Pristina hospital after a static police patrol was attacked at a bridge in the centre of Podujevo on 3rd March," on March 3rd. Do you remember that at all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall the specific incidents mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Assuming the truth of what I just read, Mr. Zyrapi, is there any conceivable set of circumstances that you can think of where attacking a static police patrol in the centre of Podujevo could qualify as a defensive action?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've mentioned earlier, there were attacks on check-points. And as I said earlier, only when our units were moving from one area to another, and if their movement was impeded, that's when these attacks were carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right. And I'll just mention one other part of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before -- before you move on. Mr. Zyrapi, you're talking about your units moving and their movement being impeded. Was there some reason in the cease-fire agreement why the MUP should not have check-points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In general where there should not have been check-points but also in territories where there were check-points and which constituted obstacles for the movement of our units from one territory to another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was it within the contemplation of the cease-fire that you should be able to move units from one area to another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When speaking of the cease-fire, there was an earlier attack in Rance, in the territory of Nerodimlje Operational Zone carried out by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, that's an entirely different point. It may well be that the Serb forces regularly breached the cease-fire for all we have yet heard. That's not what I'm asking you about. What I'm asking you about is whether the simple situation that you paint of attacking MUP check-points to enable your forces to move from one area to another was something that could be justified within the terms of the cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I speak within the framework of the cease-fire. I refer to movement by the KLA in the territories that they controlled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Just another incident and we'll be through with this line of questioning, Mr. Zyrapi. The -- contained in the report, it says: "On 5 March, approximately 15 to 20 KLA members ambushed a police patrol in an area south-west of Pristina airport. According to police sources, 11 policemen were wounded, six of them seriously, and two police vehicles were destroyed by rocket-propelled grenades." Again, do you have any recollection of this incident and would you have either approved it or ordered it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I do not remember every specific incident that occurred at that time. There are reports, but for the moment I do not recall every particular incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's the same incident as we've already dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No. I think in the others there was -- it was another incident, Your Honour, where policemen were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no. There was one on the 5th of March. Ambush of a convoy that was delivering food and rotating personnel. Is it not the same incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, I think you are right, Your Honour. Excuse me. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Mr. Zyrapi: In the report, it says: "A new area of military engagement became gradually active since the end of February as apparently the KLA from other regions moved to villages south-west of Kacanik, near the southern border with the federal FYR of Macedonia. This was followed by an increased concentration of VJ and police forces. Reports of fighting in that area were received on 28 February when the security forces were attached by the KLA near Gajre," if that's the proper pronunciation, G-a-j-r-e, "south-west of Kacanik. One police officer, the commander of the Kacanik police station, was killed, and four policemen wounded. An estimated 2.000 people fled villages in the Kacanik area, some trying to cross a border to the FYR of Macedonia." Now, I'll ask you whether the KLA was attempting to provide access for a potential NATO ground invasion of Kosovo through this Kacanik area. Was that something that you were planning during this period?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time we were not planning this, and at that time I didn't know that there would be any infantry forces of the NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, do you remember a man or do you remember meeting a man named Christopher John Clark? Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this name. What period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'm talking about this period that I just asked you about, which would have been on 28 February of 1999. Mr. Clark is a warrant officer in the British Army, and he was the Kosovo Verification Mission, KVM mission, operations officer for Kosovo. He submitted a statement - and it's 3D386 - to the Office the Prosecution in March and July of 2001, and in it he says as follows: "Also, in late February or early March, 1999, KLA forces infiltrated into the Kotlina area in southern Kosovo. This brigade had not previously been seen in Kosovo and was believed to have been infiltrated across the Macedonian border. After they came into Kosovo, we identified them and placed a team with them. It was commanded by a man known as Bardi," B-a-r-d-i, "who had previously been in the Dukagjin zone. The brigade was made up of all Macedonian Albanians. They ordered the local Kosovo Albanian population out of the area and forced them across the border into Macedonia. This was in order for them to commence an offensive against Serb forces in the area. I know this as this information was relayed to us by the brigade. The KVM assessment at the time was that the KLA was attempting to provide an access for a NATO ground invasion through this area." Does that refresh your recollection at all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. The territory that you mentioned, which was the territory that this brigade entered?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Kotlina, Kacanik, that area near the Macedonian border.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kotlina and Kacanik, this was the area of the 162nd Brigade. I don't know of any other brigade coming from the territory of Macedonia. What I know is that this brigade was here; 162 was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't know of any preparation for any kind of offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The brigade you've just referred to, the 162nd, was that composed of Macedonian Albanians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This brigade was composed of Albanians from Kosovo, from the territory of Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does the name "Bardi" mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Bardi" is the pseudonym of the commander of the 162nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what ethnicity was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: In this report that I've just been reading from - and that's 3D179 - there are a number of incidents set forth of kidnapping and abduction, and I'm not going to ask you about it because I think I know your feelings about kidnapping and abductions, which I'll ask you about now. Is it true that, by the summer -- actually, before I get to that, before I get to that, let me just finish up with -- we've taken you to January, February, and March of 1999, and I want to get into the wartime period just briefly, just very briefly, and primarily, as it relates to cooperation between the KLA and NATO. One of your zone commanders, Mr. Haradinaj, in his book, "The Story of War and Freedom," 3D375, and I might ask you if you're familiar with that book.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard about this book that Mr. Haradinaj has written.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, two excerpts from that book were attached to your 2005 statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And in that book, here's what Mr. Haradinaj says about cooperation with NATO. The question was: "How did the KLA and NATO cooperate during the bombing campaign?" And Mr. Haradinaj said: "This must be assessed realistically. From the military point of view, Kosovo was the field of action for both NATO and the KLA. These two forces were allied but hardly equal. They had common and closely connected interests with mutual." It stops there, it just says "... with mutual." "I benefited from the air-strikes, while the NATO pilots benefited from our firing lines which forced the Serbian forces out into the open. That is how we cooperated." Is that something that you agree with, Mr. Zyrapi?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because it's him who wrote that. I was not in the area at the time that he was, so I don't know what he was doing at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So you were in the area, as I understand it, through April; is that correct? You were the -- as I understand it, you were the Chief of the General Staff through April. Do I have that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not in that function through April. I left the function at about -- it was the second half of April, and then I got the duty of deputy minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: So you were there at least during a portion of the NATO bombings; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, starting from the 24th, including the second part of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. And is it also fair to say that a large portion of NATO's bombing targets in Kosovo came from the KLA commanders via satellite phone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know after April, but before April it was not like that, because the reports about our forces were sent to our ministry, which was created out of the Rambouillet talks, at the Rambouillet talks. And then after that I don't know where those reports went.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And you are familiar or do you know Baton Haxhiu, who is a Kosovo newspaper editor? Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: He was quoted in an article in The New York Review of Books on June 24th, 1999, an article called "Kosovo and Beyond," an article written by Timothy Garton Ash, who essentially says what I just asked you. He says that "a large proportion of NATO's bombing targets in Kosovo" - and, by the way, this is 3D382 - "a large proportion of NATO's bombing targets in Kosovo came from the KLA commanders via satellite phone." And is it your testimony that that is not correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I speak here about the period when I was in that duty, carrying out that function, and what we did, we sent reports to the Ministry of Defence, which was based in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reports were about our forces and the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. And so, finally, by the time the war started, at least during the time you were connected with the war, is it fair to say that you had a much stronger, regular army, without being unduly modest, due, at least, in some part to your efforts, with the capacity to use guerrilla tactics when necessary and aided by a civilian population who assisted you with food, lodging, and any other assistance they could give? Is that a pretty fair summary of the situation that existed during the war?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm just going to turn to one other area, and that is what I didn't ask you about just a few moments ago because I believe you've already indicated your attitude about this, and that is the killings and abductions of Serbian civilians and alleged Albanian collaborationists. Is it true that by the summer of 1998, it was common knowledge that Albanians were being killed because they were considered collaborators with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time I heard about these cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And these cases were also mentioned in communiques issued by the General Staff and reported in the Kosovo press, such as in papers like Bujku and Koha Ditore, et cetera; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In many communiques of the General Staff you could find these things, and also in newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And you mentioned yesterday that you also heard from zone commanders, from soldiers, and from the civilian population of maltreatment of Serbian civilians and alleged Albanian collaborationists; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated yesterday that I heard from zone commanders and civilians that some soldiers and officers had exceeded their competencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: All right. And you wanted to do something about that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I could not do anything because I did not have any function. After I became Chief of Staff, we mentioned yesterday what measures I took to discipline the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes. And after you became Chief of Staff, you entered an order - and that's Prosecution Exhibit 2448 - which essentially banned improper behaviour with respect to the civilian population; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And there were also rules about that, too; right? You testified about the KLA rules and regulations. That's Prosecution Exhibit 2499. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And you issued an order about that - and that's Prosecution Exhibit 20 - you didn't issue the order, but Prosecution Exhibit 2463, you testified yesterday, was an order by an investigating judge about what you said was investigating a serious breach. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: But you didn't remember when you testified what that breach was all about; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I did not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Do you remember now, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. There have been other cases of killings that were investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You personally know about other cases of killings of, what, Serbian civilians and alleged Albanian collaborationists? Is that a fair statement? And you know about those that have been investigated?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I personally don't know about cases of killings of Albanians or Serbs, but there have been investigations in the period of January and February. It was a very short period of time to do anything, but I know that there were investigations carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Well, you certainly read about these killings in the communiques, did you not, sir? And you heard about it from your commanders and your soldiers and civilians.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about such things, but I don't know of any specific concrete case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you: You mentioned this order yesterday, and you said you received this order from the archives of the Pastrik Operational Zone. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Now, where are the archives of the Pastrik Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them are at the General Staff of the KPC.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And tell me again what that stands for.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And some are in the zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: KPC, again, stands for what? I know you told us before, but just to --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosovo Protection Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And did you physically go to the archives in the Pastrik Operative Zone to get this document?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Again, that's located specifically where? In what village or town or city is it located?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the zone is in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And did the Prosecutor's office ask you to obtain this record and records like this?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not ask me directly, but they told me what I could testify about when I came here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And what was that? What was that conversation? When you say they told you what you could testify about, when was that? When did they tell you that? And what is it they said you could testify about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier - this was before I came here - when I gave my statement in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You said, if I'm not mistaken, that the Prosecution told you what you could testify about. Could you just be a little more precise about that. What was the conversation with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution talked with me about things that I knew that I could testify about. They did not tell me what to say here. They asked me what I knew, and come and tell the truth here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Did they ask you to find records of disciplinary actions by either a local commander or a military court against KLA soldiers who had either murdered or abducted Serbian civilians or alleged Albanian collaborationists?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said, in general, if I had any documents that I could find, documents that could be useful. They did not specify what kinds of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: But they spoke to you about that specific topic, about finding documents concerning disciplinary actions or court procedures instituted against KLA members who were suspected of killing or abducting Serb civilians or Albanian collaborationists. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not only about these ones but in general. Not only about disciplinary measures but also other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: But the conversation did include disciplinary measures; is that fair? Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of the things we talked about was disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: And so, pursuant to that discussion, you have produced here yesterday, as I understand it, two documents. One is this order that the investigating judge is to be executed [sic], making the commander of the military police responsible for the execution of the order, and then another order, as I recall, yesterday, based on the rules of discipline, confining Hasan Obej, a soldier of the KLA, to detention for a period of 48 hours. Are those the two documents that you found regarding disciplinary measures?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were two documents I obtained, and they relate to disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It should possibly be noted that it was the order of the investigating judge that was to be executed and not the investigating judge that was to be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. I can't say heads will roll on that one. My head will roll, Your Honour. Thank you for the correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Let me ask you this overall question, Mr. Zyrapi: To your knowledge, during the entire period of your being in Kosovo, from the time you came to Kosovo on May 28th, 1998, to the time you left your position in mid-April of 1998, do you personally know of a single case -- 1999 is correct. I meant April, 1999. Do you personally know of a single case in which the KLA disciplined or punished its own troops for killings or abductions of Serbian civilians or alleged Albanian collaborationists?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not personally, no, but I know that many measures were taken between January and February. But, as I said, this was a very short period of time to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: In the Limaj trial -- and, of course, you remember the Limaj trial because you were a witness for Mr. Limaj; correct? You have to say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: A witness named Peter Bouchaert, B-o-u-c-h-a-e-r-t, who was a human rights activist, testified that after a very thorough investigation, he said, "We didn't document a single case" - and this is actually, to be fair, the period between February and November of 1998 - "we didn't document a single case in which the KLA disciplined or punished their own troops despite our repeated requests for them to provide that information." And I ask you again, sir, do you personally know of a single case in which a KLA soldier was disciplined for the murder of Serbian civilians or the abduction of Serbian civilians, or the murder or abduction of alleged Albanian collaborationists? Do you personally know of a single case where that happened?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question has been answered, Mr. Sepenuk, by the witness telling you he didn't personally know of any such case. I'm beginning to wonder about the relevance of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Well, it's just I'm questioning the good-faith nature of the disciplinary measures, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the relevance of that, also, I wonder about in the overall context of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: I'll ask you one last question, Mr. Zyrapi: Are you aware of a ditch located near the village of Decani where the KLA would dispose of bodies of Serbs, informants and collaborators? Are you at all aware of that? And I will represent to you that the same gentleman I mentioned before ...

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: You're not aware. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sepenuk. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Sir, you've testified that in mid-April you became the deputy minister of defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Could you remind us who the minister of defence was?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the Defence Minister was Azim Syla.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, when was the Ministry of Defence established?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was established right after the Rambouillet talks, when the provisional government was established. So this is when the defence ministry was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: And where was the ministry located?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, it was based in Albania, in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: You said a moment ago, and earlier, that your ministry was created out of the Rambouillet talks, at the Rambouillet talks. Could you enlighten us as to how that was -- how the Rambouillet talks effected the creation of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the effect, but I know that right after the Rambouillet talks, the provisional government was established and, within its frames, the defence government -- correction, defence ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Is it your understanding that the defence ministry was discussed at Rambouillet and was created as a result of the Rambouillet talks?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, then, what connection do you -- you made a connection between Rambouillet and the creation of this Ministry of Defence. Why do you say -- why do you connect the two?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said was that after the Rambouillet talks the provisional government was formed, and within that government the Defence Minister, as part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: So that would be early March of 1999; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A little bit later the ministries began to be established. I do not know the exact time when, whether it was in early March or late March. But it is around this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zyrapi, I'm Vladimir Petrovic and I have a few questions for you. I would like to go back to the beginning of your evidence yesterday where you spoke about the fact that, in 1985, you worked on the establishment of the Albanian arm in Kosovo, and that some 30 officers and non-commissioned officers participated in this effort together with you, and that you received a suspended sentence of one and a half years in prison. Can you please tell me whether all of those 30 officers and NCOs were Albanian -- of Albanian ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The period that you mentioned, what I can speak of, at least for myself, is that we did not work as officers in the direction of forming an Albanian army, but all these 30 officers and non-commissioned officers were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would just like to remind you of what you, yourself, said yesterday. Perhaps there was a misunderstanding, but yesterday, when asked by the Prosecutor, you said the following - that's page 33 of the transcript yesterday: "[In English] We were working to form the military liberation army in Kosovo and the tribunal found us guilty and condemned us." [Interpretation] Later on, when the Presiding Judge asked the question, it was clarified that this was, in fact, an Albanian army in Kosovo. Is your evidence different from what you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it is stated in my statement - you have my statement - I did not say that we worked in the direction of establishing an army but that we were allegedly working to establish such an army. These were allegations by the court. I did not say that we worked in the direction of establishing an army, and this is clearly stated in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is contained in your statement. You did say, "allegedly, we worked on it," but yesterday it was that there were no such caveats. But we will not go into that any further. If this is your evidence today, we will accept it. Let me now move on to another area. Yesterday, you mentioned the establishment of a court as part of the General Staff of the KLA, and, among other things, you mentioned Mr. Sokol Dobruna, who had been appointed a military judge in December, 1998. My question to you is whether before this time period, anyone ever discharged any judicial function in the KLA. Did any such post exist? I mean, the post of a military judge or any other judicial authority within the General Staff of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, not until that period of time. It did not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who appointed Mr. Dobruna to this post?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was requested that a military court be formed, and following a proposal of the general commander, this is how he was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So the judge was appointed by the commander-in-chief of the KLA if that's -- if my understanding is correct. But tell me, who was the investigating judge that you mention in the document that was shown to you by my learned colleague Mr. Sepenuk? Who is that man? If it's necessary, I can give you the exact reference for the document, but I do believe that you remember the document we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the document that we're talking about and that we mentioned yesterday, but I don't remember his name, even not today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was it some other person, not Mr. Dobruna, or --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned yesterday, there were two or three other persons who were working in the military court alongside Mr. Dobruna.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. So you tell us there was a military court and the judge in the military court. Now, pursuant to what law or regulation did Dobruna or any other military judges apply in the cases that you told us about? You tell us that there were such cases, but you cannot recall any specific case.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollections, the military court abided by international conventions and the KLA rules. It was not within my competence to follow everything, but, more or less, these are the regulations that the military court abided by.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of any cases that were tried applying the KLA rules and the international conventions in which there were some convictions? It doesn't matter. Maybe you don't recall the exact name, but can you tell us whether there were any such cases at all?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such cases, but for the moment I can't remember them. And as I said, it was not within my competence to check the work of the military court and what they were involved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I have just one question related to this topic. According to your evidence, somebody who was convicted, who could that person appeal to? Was there a second instance court, or did this Dobruna deal with appeals, too? Was there a military prosecutor? What kind of a system was there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the system. As I said, it was not within my competence to see how this military court was organised. And, as I said, I do not recall cases, specific cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now let me move on to something else. As a person that was the Chief of Staff between November, 1998, and April, 1999, did you, in this capacity, initiate any investigation or any proceedings in cases where you heard reports that people were killed, tortured, kidnapped, all those things that you spoke about to my colleague Mr. Sepenuk? Did you personally launch any kind of proceedings against any KLA troops at the time when you were at the most responsible post in the Kosovo Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the most serious violations were referred to the military court. Personally, I couldn't launch any kind of proceedings against that because it was in the hands of the military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So although you did hear about kidnappings, murders, you personally did not do anything about that. You considered that to be outside of your sphere of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that question just for a moment. Mr. Petrovic, I raised this with Mr. Sepenuk already. What is the relevance of this to the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Sepenuk gave you some of the grounds for this line of questioning. Secondly, it is the intent of the Prosecution to show the Kosovo Liberation Army as a structured military organisation that would be a match for the Serbian and Yugoslav forces in Kosovo, through this witness. It is my intention to challenge this argument. If you don't consider this to be relevant, I can move on, because this was, indeed, the last question related to this topic anyway. So I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You surprise me that it assists -- that you think it assists the Prosecution to demonstrate the Kosovo Liberation Army to be particularly structured. Indeed, I thought it was a stronger Defence point than a Prosecution one. These questions seem to me, but I am not really in a position to judge, to be rather undermining than enhancing your case at the moment. But lay that aside, I really don't understand the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, Your Honour. I will move on, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As regards the General Staff, can you please tell us when it was established, the General Staff of the Kosovo Liberation Army, if you know until?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when exactly it was formed. It was formed in that capacity much earlier, and I can only speak of the period of time when I was appointed to that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who established it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was established earlier, when the Kosovo Liberation Army was being formed. Among those who participated in the establishment of the General Staff was Azim Syla, who held that duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Okay. But, to your knowledge, is there a decision to establish the General Staff and the various organs within the staff? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there a civilian organ that oversaw the work of the Kosovo Liberation Army General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for the earlier times, but when the political directorate was formed, later on, in January and February.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You're talking about the political leadership of the KLA. I'm asking you whether there was any authority outside of the KLA that would be running the working of the KLA or controlling the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was formed out of the Kosovo Popular Movement, the LPK. The staff derived from this party, and it was controlled by this party, to the information that I had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me whether you know that, on several occasions in Kosovo, there were elections that were not recognised but were tolerated by the Serbian authorities? So there was an assembly; there was the president of Kosovo. Did they have any influence over the activities of the KLA? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about this, but I don't know about their activities during this period of time. And there was nobody overseeing the KLA at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to ask you something about the political goals of the KLA. Is it correct that the KLA saw Kosovo and Metohija solely as the occupied part of the territory of the Republic of Albania? Was this the political views of the KLA at the time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what view prevailed earlier, but during that time that I held that post, Kosovo was considered as an occupied territory but not as part of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In this context I would like to read out to you a part of Exhibit P2449. These are interim provisions on the internal structure of the army. Right at the beginning of this document, we have the military oath. This is the document we looked at yesterday; you confirmed its authenticity. It says here - that's section 2, paragraph 1 - and I read: "As a member of the Kosovo Liberation Army, I swear that I will fight for the liberation of the occupied territories of Albania and their unification." This is what it says in the military oath taken by the soldiers of the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated yesterday as well that there were changes that were made with the oath and the salute. I'm not saying that this did not exist earlier, but at least for the period that I was at the post of Chief of General Staff, this was not used.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So it was not used. I have just two more questions. In this period that we are now talking about when you were the Chief of Staff, did you have any foreign advisors? Were there any people who assisted in the training, the setting up of communications, the organisation of the Kosovo Liberation Army, people from the outside? Also, in equipping it.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my time in office, I did not have foreign advisors coming from foreign states.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contacts with any other army, any other service at the time when you were the Chief of General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not during my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Marcussen, is it necessary to interrupt the evidence of this witness to lead a different witness tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's our request, to start with the witness Baton Haxhiu first thing tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the estimated timing for him?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller told me she thought she would take 45 minutes to an hour on direct. I don't know how long the Defence estimates for cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's also quite a lengthy statement from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So when should Mr. Zyrapi return?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the estimate from the Defence is as for cross-examine. I understood from an earlier conversation that we thought we'd be done with him in two sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, can you help? Or should I look to Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Ivetic would answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is for Mr. Zyrapi? Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're talking about the likely length of cross of Mr. Baton Haxhiu.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's my witness, Your Honour. As I indicated to Mr. Hannis, at present, I have about 30 or 40 minutes worth of cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Well, Mr. Zyrapi, we need to interrupt now for today, and we are being invited to hear a different witness for at least part of tomorrow, probably the bulk of tomorrow, but you, nevertheless, need to be here in anticipation that during the latter part of the day you will be able to resume your evidence, possibly even finish it, although I can't say that for sure. So you should be back here, ready to resume, at 5.00 tomorrow. Meanwhile, it's vital, as I said to you yesterday, that you do not discuss any aspect of your evidence with anyone at all. Otherwise, enjoy the evening and return here ready to resume, if we can arrange it, at 5.00 tomorrow. Could you please now leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If Your Honour would allow me one brief thing. I should have done this earlier, but I am seeing what is probably going to be the notorious "A, B, C map" lying on the usher's desk. Maybe it would be a good idea if we make it an in-court exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I think I forgot to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now that I'm on my feet, maybe just one correction. At page 74, line 9, of today's transcript, Mr. Sepenuk made reference to a Prosecution exhibit as being Prosecution Exhibit P2499. That should have been P2449. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC105, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn now until 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
